title: capacity-heuristics-and-ops-journal-2029-06-11
content:
Context:
This is a working weekly journal for capacity heuristics and operational observations. Primary focus this week: rolling adjustments to priming windows, a short experiment on opportunistic backfill, and an incident triage from 2029-06-09 that revealed a regional preemption pattern impacting dedicated slots. Notes are intentionally informal — working checklist + outcomes + questions for design review.

Attendees / quick notes:
- Asha (owner) — ran capacity playbook run-through, coordinated with oncall.
- Diego — telemetry and heatmap updates, wrote quick metric query.
- Leah — priming config experiments, traffic replay.
- Omar — preemption root-cause analysis, cloud provider liaison.
- Priya — Dedicated customer impact triage, notification drafts.

Highlights this week:
- Small incident (06-09) where NA-west preemptible backfill caused 3k request failures across low-tier routes over a 12-minute window. Failures were concentrated on dedicated slots that had burst policy enabled.
- Ran a controlled priming-heuristic AB test: widened priming window by +30s for cold-start-heavy models and lowered slot expiry threshold from 90s -> 60s for opportunistic backfill lanes. Observed 8% lower median tail latency for sequences <128 tokens in NA-west during test period.
- Launched a lightweight queueing experiment (degraded fairness) to allow short-lived customer requests to preempt long-running batch jobs in EU-central only. Early results: throughput up 2.7% but 0.9% increase in long-tail latency for batching customers.

Regional snapshots (quick numbers, rough):
- NA-west: spare-capacity ~6.5% (was 4.0% before priming tweak), mean generation latency 62ms (models small-medium), preemption events 0.28/hr calendar day (down from 0.6/hr after mitigation).
- EU-central: spare-capacity ~4.1%, observed batch/backfill contention during peak 11:00-14:00 UTC.
- APAC-sg: spare-capacity ~9.8% (overprovisioned intentionally for APAC launch), but queueing jitter observed during spike on 06-07.

Incident triage summary (06-09 NA-west):
- Symptom: sudden increase in request errors with provider code 429/503. Correlated with large backfill job that started at 15:18 PDT.
- Root cause hypothesis: provider preemption of opportunistic instances + our burst policy allowed eviction of dedicated-similar slots (config drift in autoscaler).
- Short-term mitigation applied: disabled opportunistic backfill for tier=dedicated routes; forced-conservative autoscaler cooldown (jira/INFRA-1342).
- Longer-term action: add cross-check in autoscaler that prevents opportunistic label assignment if active dedicated slots count > X% (see action items).

Heuristics & experiments (notes):
1) Priming window tuning: current baseline = 45s. Experiment: +30s for models with cold-start frequency > 12% per hour. Result: reduces first-token latency variance for those models, but increases transient slot occupancy ~5%. Tradeoff acceptable for user-facing low-latency APIs.
2) Slot expiry threshold change: lowering expiry to 60s cleans opportunistic churn. Side effect: slightly increased RPC rate because more new allocations — observed ~3% more allocation API calls. Need to monitor rate limits.
3) Opportunistic backfill fairness test (EU-central): allowing short requests to displace long-running background batches improved tail latency for interactive customers but degraded batch SLO. Decision: roll forward in EU-central only with explicit route tags for batch-sensitive customers.

Operational playbook updates (what I changed in the doc during the meeting):
- Added a preemption scoreboard metric (preemptions per 1k slot-hours) and a new alert threshold at 0.5 (was 1.0).
- New runbook step: automated rollback trigger when dedicated route error-rate increases >2x baseline within 10 minutes of priming change.

Action items (owner — due):
- Omar — add autoscaler label guard (jira/INFRA-1409) — due 2029-06-18.
- Diego — roll updated heatmap query into dashboards + create preemption scoreboard panel — due 2029-06-13.
- Leah — run full 48h priming-window soak for 3 representative models (small/medium/large) and post artifacts — due 2029-06-20.
- Priya — notify affected Dedicated customers of policy changes, prepare FAQ draft — due 2029-06-14.
- Asha — draft proposal for cross-region priming policy (centralized guardrails + regional override) and share with product/console — due 2029-06-21.

Risks / unresolved questions:
- How aggressive should we be with slot expiry reductions before we blow through API allocation quotas? Current safety buffer is thin for some regions.
- Can we add a simulated provider-preemption trace to the staging environment so we can rehearse? Low confidence in replays reproducing timing.
- Batch customers have voiced concerns about fairness; need clearer opt-in/opt-out semantics in route config.

Notes for review meeting with product (scheduled 2029-06-15):
- Prepare latency vs cost delta for priming window +30s (goal: show gross savings if we reduce downstream retries by x%).
- Present the preemption scoreboard and the autoscaler guard proposal.
- Include customer impact summary for Dedicated customers on 06-09 incident.

Quick links and references (working):
- Incident runbook snapshot: jira/INFRA-1342
- Autoscaler guard proposal draft: github/prs/infra/replace-priming-signal-187
- Dashboards: grafana://infra-capacity/priming-heatmap (private)
- Slack thread: slack://thread/CF0ABCDE/incident-06-09

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider a small randomized jitter on slot expiry to avoid synchronized churn when multiple regions pick same thresholds.
- Re-evaluate priming for very large models (>512k tokens) separately; current heuristics centered on small/medium.
- If preemption scoreboard goes red, auto-suppress opportunistic backfill across all regions until manual review.

End of week reflection: felt like a week of incremental wins — small latency improvements and better observability. The incident highlighted a configuration coupling we didn't expect; fix will require both code (autoscaler guard) and policy (dedicated vs opportunistic boundaries). I'll push the autoscaler guard to top of the queue next sprint and coordinate the outreach.
